newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran calls for anti-Israel rally by Moslem pilgrims.
newsitem.headline: Iran calls for anti-Israel rally by Moslem pilgrims.

text.p: Iranian state radio on Tuesday urged Moslems to stage a rally at the annual haj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia to protest at Israel's policies in Jerusalem.

"Now that...problems such as attempts by the Zionist regime (Israel) to occupy Jerusalem permanently have led to a joint cry of protest (by Moslems), it is more necessary than ever to take advantage of the great haj gathering to raise their voices in disavowal of the infidels," Tehran radio said.

It was referring in a commentary to the "disavowal of infidels" rally, banned by conservative Sunni Saudi Arabia, which radical Shi'ite Iran says pilgrims should hold to denounce Israel and the United States as enemies of Islam.
About two million Moslems -- half of them from outside Saudi Arabia -- are expected to perform this year's haj at Mecca, site of Islam's holiest shrine. The haj reaches its climax next week.

"The Islamic world's enemies are watching this year's haj with sensitivity and anxiousness, because Moslems from the world's farthest points, inspired by (Iran's 1979) Islamic revolution..., may use the opportunity provided by haj to protest at the policies of arrogant (Western) powers and the Zionist regime," the radio said.
Saudi Arabia's King Fahd urged pilgrims on Monday to avoid politics during the haj. Saudi Arabia has reiterated it would deal harshly with violators of the ban on political activity.

The warnings appear aimed at Iran, which says Moslems have the right to air political grievances during haj, mainly through rallies against the United States and Israel. Saudi Arabia says haj is purely religious and should not be politicised.
Iran boycotted haj for three years after some 400 people, mainly Iranian pilgrims, were killed in clashes in 1987 between Saudi police and Iranians holding a political rally in Mecca.
The row over haj usually further strains already tense relations between the two powerful regional oil producers.

Iran has been trying to improve ties with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Arab states. Iranian media and officials have used a softer tone towards the kingdom in recent weeks even when calling for rallies during the pilgrimage.
